value.rationale: The truncated-tetrahedral graph is a canonical Archimedean cubic graph with a natural directed-tetrahedral-edge encoding; its exact temporal census is a motivated finite dynamical invariant. The 6 primitive period-eight cycles form one S4 orbit and excite every vertex twice, whereas the 6 period-four cycles form another orbit with excitation once per vertex. Hence equal rate 1/4 coexists with different least periods, exposing a structural distinction invisible to the classical common-activity invariant. Full basin/entry counts give a reproducible finite benchmark; no general theorem is claimed.
